editorial:
You follow two cousins, David and Benji, on a guided tour through Poland to honor their beloved grandmother. They are very different: David is careful, anxious, and always planning, while Benji is loud, loose, and says whatever he feels. Their old family tension shows up during the group trip, especially when memories of their grandmother and family history come up. It mixes laughs with sad moments, feeling like a road trip with real heart and a lot of awkward honesty.

Acting feels natural and emotional, especially the cousins' back-and-forth and the way small moments say a lot. Pacing is steady, not rushed, with quiet scenes that let feelings land without dragging. Some jokes may feel awkward, and a few side characters get little time. If you like character stories with humor, grief, and family drama, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, David and Benji finally say what they have been holding back. Benji decides to stay in Poland a little longer, while David heads home to his family. The last moments show David back in normal life, still carrying their shared grief, but with a clearer bond and more understanding between them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven stories with humor and grief.
